headline: A 2014 law requires Medicare post-acute care providers to report standardized patient data, links the reporting to Medicare payment changes, and adds hospice oversight rules.
what_it_does: The law directs the Health and Human Services Secretary to require home health agencies, inpatient rehabilitation facilities, long-term care hospitals, and skilled nursing facilities to report standardized patient assessment, quality, and resource-use data. Skilled nursing facilities that do not report get a 2% reduction in their annual payment update. The law also requires hospices to receive a standard survey at least every 36 months and adds medical review for long-stay hospice patients. It replaces an older Medicare fund with a new Medicare Improvement Fund for fee-for-service improvements.

who_it_affects.group: Medicare beneficiaries who use home health, rehabilitation, long-term care hospital, or skilled nursing care
who_it_affects.how: Their providers will report more standardized data, which the law says is meant to help care be coordinated when they move between settings, including at discharge.

who_it_affects.group: Home health agencies, inpatient rehabilitation facilities, and long-term care hospitals
who_it_affects.how: They must report quality, resource-use, and standardized patient assessment data on a three-phase schedule.
Those that do not report the required data will have their annual market basket payment update reduced by 2%.

who_it_affects.group: Hospice programs and their long-stay patients
who_it_affects.how: Hospices face surveys at least every 36 months, and patients receiving hospice care for more than 180 days may face medical review if the share of such patients is high.
A re-established Medicare Improvement Fund, funded from both Medicare trust funds, can be used by the Secretary for fee-for-service improvements starting in and after fiscal year 2020.

when_it_takes_effect: The reporting requirements phase in on a three-phase schedule set by the Secretary. Hospice survey funding runs from fiscal years 2015 through 2025, and the hospice payment cap update applies for fiscal years 2017 through 2025. The Medicare Improvement Fund is available during and after fiscal year 2020.
